result.title: Latent-Predisposition Personas for Heterogeneous and Reliable LLM Survey Simulation
result.summary: LLM personas are used to simulate survey publics, which should reproduce not only answer distributions but also within-person coherence and stability. Drawing on mass belief systems research, we show that persona-conditioned LLMs produce over-constrained publics. Across three model families and three U.S. surveys, opinions on unrelated issues are 1.6-4.6 times as correlated as among humans, and party identification explains 2.5-7.6 times as much answer variance. Common remedies (temperature, diversity instructions, backstories) weaken these correlations by making answers more random. On Qwen, their ten-day test-retest reliability falls to 33-59% of the human level, and when made consistent they lose correlation fit. We propose Latent-Predisposition Personas (LPP), whose persons differ stably, not randomly. Each persona receives political engagement, value priorities, and party-relative issue deviations that grow as engagement falls. Answers are sharpened and calibrated to toplines and party crosstabs. At selected operating points, LPP is never significantly worse than any baseline and far more reliable. At matched human-level reliability, it has the lowest correlation error in all six model-survey combinations, also at a lower target. Errors still exceed those between human samples, and gains on framing effects and a frontier closed model are partial.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究用 LLM 模拟调查公众，指出现有 persona 条件化会产生过度一致、相关性强于真人的回答，并提出 Latent-Predisposition Personas：为每个 persona 分配潜在倾向参数（政治参与度、价值优先级、党际议题偏差），再将答案锐化并校准到总体与交叉表分布。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用少量潜在倾向变量换取稳定而非随机的个体差异，并校准到聚合统计」的思路，可能与 LVR 中 latent 状态参数化、表示稳定性与解码校准的可核查线索有关，但领域相距较远。
